searchText: Hi, can someone tell me when are we expecting the results for the mainnet shadow fork? Is there a place I can go to for following the outcome/results? The transition to PoS should be on Monday and the I think the beaconchain genesis is today. Beaconchain genesis in just under 6 hours 👌 An update on the Transition test coverage, I have finished incorporating Engine API reqs into testing scenarios, https://hackmd.io/vjgC9hV_TrK1ZuftVm1rZA?view#Transition -- they worth checking now. Some of them are already marked as done cc <@!892053833121923094> It seems like I have also found a blind spot in the spec. Suppose there is a chain `TB <- INV_P0 <- P1 <- P2 <- ... <- Pn`, where `TB` is a valid terminal block, `INV_P0` is an invalid payload of a transition block. It's not that clear what EL should respond with to `newPayload(INV_P0)` call: - `{status: INVALID, latestValidHash: TB.blockHash, validationError: errorMessage | null}` -- but `TB.blockHash` doesn't make any sense to CL - `{status: INVALID_TERMINAL_BLOCK, latestValidHash: null, validationError: errorMessage | null}` -- but terminal block is valid, though, this effectively will invalidate the chain starting from `INV_P0` if for instance this chain was the one a node is in sync with and would like to be able to invalidate such a chain from the very beginning This is another input to the recent `latestValidHash` discussion Will check it now, thanks 🙏 We are also having a discussion on a test case that originated from the modifications to increase coverage: - Send `fcU(A)` where payload `A` is missing, which leads client to `SYNCING` state - Send `newPayload(B)` where `B.parentHash==A.hash`, `B` extends canonical chain because of the previous `fcU` - Test expects `SYNCING` response from `newPayload(B)` because of this part in the exec spec: `{status: SYNCING, latestValidHash: null, validationError: null} if the payload extends the canonical chain and requisite data for its validation is missing` - All clients are currently responding with `ACCEPTED` instead of `SYNCING` because the original `fcU(A)` is not cached Gentlemen, I'd love to test this for geth2 0 but I need 32geth. I got very little goerli at the faucet for a few days. What's the better way to get goerli <@456226577798135808> DM me your address hello, while running the mainnet shadow fork i noticed i am getting the following logs on prysm: ``` `[2022-04-08 23:41:00] ERROR powchain: Could not log ttd status error=empty hex string got an unexpected error github.com/prysmaticlabs/prysm/beacon-chain/powchain.handleRPCError beacon-chain/powchain/engine_client.go:215 github.com/prysmaticlabs/prysm/beacon-chain/powchain.(*Service).LatestExecutionBlock beacon-chain/powchain/engine_client.go:191 github.com/prysmaticlabs/prysm/beacon-chain/powchain.(*Service).logTtdStatus beacon-chain/powchain/check_transition_config.go:121 github.com/prysmaticlabs/prysm/beacon-chain/powchain.(*Service).checkTransitionConfiguration beacon-chain/powchain/check_transition_config.go:88 runtime.goexit GOROOT/src/runtime/asm_amd64.s:1581 ``` I am using Erigon, is anyone having similar issues? or is this a known behaviour? EL seems to be returning an expected response and i have no idea what `empty hex string`mean, but i suspect the response is invalid according to prysm, even though curling it give an expected result but i might be wrong

excerpts.author: m.kalinin
excerpts.content:
It seems like I have also found a blind spot in the spec.

Suppose there is a chain `TB <- INV_P0 <- P1 <- P2 <- ... <- Pn`, where `TB` is a valid terminal block, `INV_P0` is an invalid payload of a transition block.
It's not that clear what EL should respond with to `newPayload(INV_P0)` call:
- `{status: INVALID, latestValidHash: TB.blockHash, validationError: errorMessage | null}` -- but `TB.blockHash` doesn't make any sense to CL
- `{status: INVALID_TERMINAL_BLOCK, latestValidHash: null, validationError: errorMessage | null}` -- but terminal block is valid, though, this effectively will invalidate the chain starting from `INV_P0` if for instance this chain was the one a node is in sync with and would like to be able to invalidate such a chain from the very beginning

This is another input to the recent `latestValidHash` discussion

excerpts.author: marioevz
excerpts.content:
We are also having a discussion on a test case that originated from the modifications to increase coverage:
- Send `fcU(A)` where payload `A` is missing, which leads client to `SYNCING` state
- Send `newPayload(B)` where `B.parentHash==A.hash`, `B` extends canonical chain because of the previous `fcU`
- Test expects `SYNCING` response from  `newPayload(B)` because of this part in the exec spec:
`{status: SYNCING, latestValidHash: null, validationError: null} if the payload extends the canonical chain and requisite data for its validation is missing`
- All clients are currently responding with `ACCEPTED` instead of `SYNCING` because the original `fcU(A)` is not cached
